newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least five killed in Colombian prison riots.
newsitem.headline: At least five killed in Colombian prison riots.

text.p: At least five inmates were killed and nearly 30 others were injured on Thursday in prison riots in Bogota and Colombia's central Tolima province, authorities said.

The worst bloodshed occurred before dawn in Bogota's ageing Modelo prison. Rafael Lamo, head of the National Prisons Institute, said four inmates were killed and 21 injured in an uprising that began shortly after midnight Wednesday.
Lamo did not specify the causes of the deaths and injuries. But an aide said the riot began when inmates stormed a sentry post and seized a guard's rifle.
Guards moved to put down the riot about two hours later, the prison official said, adding that some of the victims were believed to have been killed or injured by fellow inmates and not guards.
"We believe there was fighting among the inmates themselves," he said, noting that some prisoners suffered knife wounds and not injuries from the guns or tear gas canisters fired by guards.

Spokesmen for the Prisons Institute later reported that six inmates and one guard were injured in a riot that broke out Thursday morning in the Picalena prison in Tolima province. One of the prisoners later died of his injuries in a regional hospital.

The Bogota riot, the worst in several months, prompted the government to declare a de facto state of emergency throughout Colombia's prison system, which has been rocked by at least a dozen major uprisings against overcrowding and poor living conditions so far this year.

Lamo said emergency measures would include curbs on visiting rights. Government officials said there would also be an effort to reduce overcrowding in the Modelo and other penitentiaries by transferring inmates to less crowded facilties.
The Modelo was built to house no more than 1,900 inmates but its current population exceeds 4,500, according to the Prisons Institute.
